source_caption:
Paul Greengrass and Tom Hanks completely subverted the traditional Hollywood rescue by ending the film with an agonizingly intimate portrait of real trauma. The woman treating Hanks in the devastating final scene wasn’t a professional actress, but an actual, active-duty Navy Corpsman named Danielle Albert. Instructed by Greengrass to simply run through her standard clinical procedure on camera, she inadvertently anchored one of the greatest pieces of improvised acting in modern cinema. As the adrenaline finally evaporates, Hanks masterfully physicalizes the terrifying onset of profound shock, proving that surviving a harrowing ordeal isn’t about walking away like an unfazed action hero—it’s the crushing, hyperventilating realization that you only barely survived.
⠀
Captain Phillips (2013), directed by Paul Greengrass, starring Tom Hanks, Barkhad Abdi. The gripping true story of the 2009 hijacking of the U.S. container ship Maersk Alabama by a crew of desperate Somali pirates.

source_details.synopsis: Captain Phillips is a 2013 American biographical action-thriller film directed by Paul Greengrass. Based on the 2009 Maersk Alabama hijacking, the film tells the story of Captain Richard Phillips, an American merchant mariner who was taken hostage by Somali pirates. It stars Tom Hanks as Phillips, alongside Barkhad Abdi as pirate leader Abduwali Muse. The screenplay by Billy Ray is based on Phillips's 2010 book A Captain's Duty: Somali Pirates, Navy SEALs, and Dangerous Days at Sea, which Phillips co-wrote with Stephan Talty.
